Dr. '''James Robinson''' (born 1948, Maine) is an American [[filk music]] [[songwriter]] and performer (known as '''Dr. Jane Robinson''' prior to 2004 [[sex reassignment surgery]]) whose songs focus on [[science|scientific themes]], particularly [[paleontology]].

Robinson earned a [[Ph.D.|doctorate]] in [[biology]] from [[UCLA]] in 1976, and went on to teach at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].

His  filk albums include ''Dr. Jane's Science Notes'' (later reissued as ''Wackademia''), ''Fossil Fever'', ''Bedlam Cats'', ''Midlife Crisis'' and ''Dr. Jane's Remains''.

Robinson has won two [[Pegasus Award]]s (2000, Best End of the World Song, for "Out of a Clear Blue Sky"; and 1992, Best Writer/Composer); and has been nominated an additional 14 times.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ovff.org/pegasus/people/jane-robinson.html |title=Pegasus Awards: J. Robinson |website=Ovff.org |date= |access-date=2013-12-03}}</ref> Robinson was inducted into the [[Filk Hall of Fame]] in 2000.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.filkontario.ca/hof/inductees/robinsondrj.html |title=Robinson's induction into the Filk Hall of Fame |website=Filkontario.ca |date= |access-date=2013-12-03 |archive-date=2013-12-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131208220925/http://www.filkontario.ca/hof/inductees/robinsondrj.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Robinson's life partner was the late [[Cynthia McQuillin]], who reportedly said, upon meeting James for the first time, "At last I get to meet the man I fell in love with!" He lives in [[Oakland, California|Oakland]], [[California]].<ref>[http://www.lasfs.org/upimages/Loscon/LC34ProgramBook.pdf LosCon 34 Program book] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304031437/http://www.lasfs.org/upimages/Loscon/LC34ProgramBook.pdf |date=2016-03-04 }} (page 64)</ref>

A book of songs by Robinson as "Dr. Jane", ''Dr. Jane's Songs'' ("all of Dr. Jane's songs that Dr. Jim Robinson could find in his archives, plus a few that Lee Gold found from other sources"), was compiled and published by [[Lee Gold]] in 2012.<ref name="songbook">[http://conchord.org/xeno/drjane.html Dr. Jane's Songs], [[Lee Gold]], ed.</ref>

== Guest of Honor appearances ==
Robinson has been a Guest of Honor (or similar position, e.g., Toastmaster) at over half a dozen conventions, including both filk-music-specific conventions:

* Counterpoint Too!<ref name="JRCToo">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nefilk.us/pastcons.shtml |title=Past Northeast Filk Conventions |access-date=2014-04-24 |archive-date=2016-04-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422014418/http://www.nefilk.us/pastcons.shtml |url-status=dead }}</ref> (the second NEFilk con)
* [[FilKONtario]] 2003<ref name="JRFKO">{{Cite web |url=http://www.other-worlds-cafe.com/news/newsletter/news_dtl.php?id=51 |title=The Other*Worlds*Cafe: News: Newsletter: February 2003 |access-date=2014-04-24 |archive-date=2016-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304024946/http://www.other-worlds-cafe.com/news/newsletter/news_dtl.php?id=51 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* Consonance 1994<ref name="JRconso">{{Cite web |url=http://www.textfiles.com/magazines/HTOMC/htomc.025 |title=Archived copy |access-date=2014-04-24 |archive-date=2005-02-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050220173951/http://www.textfiles.com/magazines/HTOMC/htomc.025 |url-status=dead }}</ref> (Toastmaster, responsible for introducing other guests but also entertaining the membership with a concert performance),
and non-filk conventions:
* Marcon 39<ref name="JRmarcon">{{cite web |url=http://www.analogsf.com/0407_08/events_07_08.shtml |title=Analog—Upcoming Events |website=Analogsf.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040604150007/http://www.analogsf.com/0407_08/events_07_08.shtml |archive-date=2004-06-04}}</ref>
* [[Capricon]] XXIV<ref name="JRcapric">{{Cite web|url=http://www.locusmag.com/2004/Future/Conventions.html|title = Locus Online: 2004 Convention Listings|website=Locusmag.com}}</ref>
* [[Norwescon]] XVII<ref name="JRNorwest">{{Cite web|url=http://www.norwescon.org/about/history/|title=History|website=Norwescon.org|date=30 May 2011}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.lasfsinc.info/loscon/34/index.html|title=LOSCON 34: The Dig|website=Lasfsinc.info|access-date=27 May 2023|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304083159/http://www.lasfsinc.info/loscon/34/index.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
